A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Chain-of-Frames research and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-C. Content can be matched across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoF model evaluations, training-data and prompting ablations, and frame-reference analyses in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original CoF evaluations and adds experiments with Phi-3.5-Vision-4B, including aggregate and task-level results in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The data-generation pipeline, frame-index reasoning, and CoF fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. Phi-3.5-Vision is an additional application of the existing procedure; no new CoF component, objective, or algorithmic adaptation is specified.

E1.justification: Both versions train on VIDEOESPRESSO and CLEVRER and evaluate on VSI-BENCH, VIDEO-MME, MVBENCH, VIDHAL, EVENTHALLUSION, and NEXTQA. NEXTQA already appeared in v1 Appendix B. The Phi experiments reuse existing benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 4-8 add Phi-3.5-Vision-4B with standard and CoT prompting as comparators for its CoF variant. The existing InternVL, external video-LLM, M-LLM, and Video-of-Thought comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v2 extends evaluation to the Phi-3.5-Vision-4B configuration and introduces an across-benchmark average in Table 1. Existing benchmark splits, individual metrics, and InternVL training budgets remain unchanged. The newly stated 30-frame inference sampling is additional documentation, not an established change to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds an explicit test of whether CoF generalizes beyond InternVL using Phi-3.5-Vision. It removes the CoF-4B frame-reference distribution and its 68.7% reference-use finding from Figure 7, retaining the 8B analysis. Existing data-source ablations, prompting comparisons, and qualitative examples largely remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The results continue to use point estimates.

E6.justification: CoF-InternVL3-8B's reported VIDEO-MME and MVBENCH scores change from 75.3 and 90.4 in v1 Table 2 to 73.7 and 77.1 in v2 Table 1, with revised appendix breakdowns. VIDEO-MME leadership consequently changes. v2 also adds Phi results throughout Tables 4-8. These are substantial reporting changes; the PDFs do not establish why the earlier scores were revised.

T1.justification: The MRA definition and threshold set in Appendix A.2 are unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions, proofs, or formal derivations beyond the retained metric description.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly claims the first single-stage video LLM reasoning with frame references and foregrounds synthetic-to-real transfer. The claim of leading VIDEO-MME, MVBENCH, and VSI-BENCH narrows to the latter two, with VIDEO-MME now second-best. The central contribution remains efficient, temporally grounded CoF reasoning.

C2.justification: The limitations shift from untested architectures beyond InternVL to fixed-FPS compatibility and unresolved adaptation to dynamic-frame-rate models such as Qwen2.5-VL. v2 more strongly interprets synthetic-data results as task transfer across distributions. It retains the general data-overlap caveat but removes v1's specific note about InternVL2.5 pretraining on CLEVRER.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies uniform sampling of 30 inference frames regardless of video duration. Appendix A.3 adds Phi's indexed image-token explanation and fine-tuning details. Existing InternVL hardware, learning rate, batch size, epoch count, and the code-link destination remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 sharpens the single-stage versus multi-stage positioning and adds references to Phi-3, Flexible Frame Selection, VidHalluc, and VideoTree. References to BGE-M3 and Grounding DINO are removed with the corresponding detailed discussion. These are limited changes around the retained comparison with prior video-reasoning methods.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory framing, related-work taxonomy, method motivation, and synthetic-data discussion are extensively rewritten. Main comparisons precede ablations, additional analyses become Section 5, and the previously supplementary video-CoT comparison moves into the main text.

P2.justification: The paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, moves Figure 1 before the abstract, relocates the full data-distribution figure to the appendix, and redisplays its combined-data pie in the main text. Tables gain average and Phi entries, and Figure 7 loses its 4B panel. Figure 1 is redrawn with an accuracy axis inconsistent with the tabulated scores.

improvement.justification: Phi evaluation and clearer inference and applicability documentation strengthen v2. However, new reporting inconsistencies affect central comparisons: Tables 4 and 7 give 74.3 and 72.5 for the same InternVL3 CoT MVBENCH baseline; Table 2 reports a 7.8-point gain although 73.7 minus 66.5 is 7.2; and Figure 1's revised accuracy axis contradicts the tables. These regressions coexist with useful additions, preventing a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
